claim: Putting hypotheses in rows and evidence in columns cut confirm-only strategy in a randomized human study (N=161); the ACH-style layout (hypotheses in columns) and per-hypothesis prose did not. Per-layout percentages (61.8/39.2/67.3% confirm-only) remain unverified: OSF holds only the 2016 pilot data, not the 2024 layout data.
agent_test: Run Dhami Task 1 (2 hyps, 12 evidence, counts so confirm-only picks A) on the agent in HypRow, HypCol, HypText layouts, many seeds, equal tokens; compare share choosing B.

claim: The row advantage is not replicated; the study was not preregistered, used mostly female students, two hypotheses, one decisive task.
agent_test: Replicate with 3-6 hypotheses and varied item counts on the agent.

claim: Layout changed which strategy was used but not sensitivity to evidence credibility (77/78/75% switched).
agent_test: Run Tasks 3A/3B on the agent per layout; check switch rate.

claim: Trained-free analysts given the ACH layout mostly balanced evidence (66.1% BAL, 19.4% CONS), so confirmation bias in analysts is weaker than assumed; the result differs from students.
agent_test: Compare weak vs strong model on same layout; analogue of student/analyst gap.

claim: CRT predicted strategy in students (d=0.54) but not in analysts (d=0.10); individual-difference links do not transfer across samples.
agent_test: Check whether a reasoning-effort setting predicts strategy in the agent.

claim: Nobody has manipulated the mechanism of the row advantage (working memory, processing order, reading direction); all three are untested.
agent_test: Ablate: sequential per-hypothesis calls vs one-shot matrix to separate order from layout.

claim: ACH training/matrix use gave mixed or no benefit in two RCTs (50 UK analysts; 191 law students; about a third used the matrix).
agent_test: Compare scaffold with and without ACH matrix step at equal tokens.

claim: For LLMs, the serialization of the same table (HTML, Markdown, JSON, NL) changes accuracy by many points; HTML was best for GPT-3.5 on size detection (67.0 vs 40.7-43.7).
agent_test: Render the S4 evidence table in 3-4 serializations on the agent; measure accuracy.

claim: Row shuffling and transposing a table lower LLM accuracy: direct prompting 59.50 to 52.21 (shuffle) and 51.14 (transpose), 37.51 both; a Python agent collapses to 12.45 when transposed. (b11 swapped the two labels; corrected.)
agent_test: Test orientation (hyp rows vs cols) on the agent in both text and code-execution modes.

claim: LLMs cannot reliably detect a bad table orientation (GPT-3.5 correct on 32.5% of transposed tables); a normalizer recovers most loss (58.66 vs 59.50 original).
agent_test: Add a normalize-layout step before S4 and see if variance across layouts shrinks.

claim: Meaning-preserving prompt format changes shift accuracy substantially (up to 76 points LLaMA-2-13B; median spread 7.5 points; GPT-3.5 up to 56), and size/instruction tuning do not remove it.
agent_test: Report a format-spread interval for every agent benchmark claim.

claim: Best prompt format differs by model (GPT-3.5 prefers JSON, GPT-4 Markdown); formats do not transfer across model series (IoU below 0.2).
agent_test: Pick layout per model by a small pilot, never copy across models.

claim: Premise order matters: forward order matching the proof is best; shuffling costs up to 20-30% (GPT-4-turbo 94.1 to 85.0 on R-GSM); weaker models lose more.
agent_test: Order evidence in proof order in S4 vs random order; equal tokens.

claim: Position effects: info in the middle of the context is used worst (over 20% drop, below closed-book 56.1% in worst case for GPT-3.5). Newer work (2025-2026): the U-shape is strongest when input fills up to about half the window and is model- and filler-specific; some current models show no middle drop.
agent_test: Place decisive evidence at start/end of S4 table vs middle.

claim: Option-position/ID bias: models favour certain option slots (llama-30B A/B/C/D 34.6/27.3/22.3/15.8%).
agent_test: Shuffle hypothesis labels and order across runs and vote.

claim: Forcing structured output (JSON/XML) lowers reasoning accuracy; answer-before-reason schema removed CoT in 100% of GPT-3.5 JSON-mode cases on Last Letter.
agent_test: Compare free-text reasoning then structured table vs structured-only output.

claim: Text vs image table form depends on model and dataset; no general winner.
agent_test: Keep text tables; skip images.

claim: An ACH consistency matrix inside an LLM pipeline added little (+0.8 points) beyond filtering plus suspect profiling (63.8 to 70.5 to 71.3 on MuSR); gain was from attention quality, not the matrix.
agent_test: Ablate matrix step in our own pipeline at equal tokens; one source, a 2026 preprint.

claim: Self-consistency with 5 samples (63.2) gave less than structured analysis (71.3), and filtering alone matched it (63.8).
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of voting vs structured filtering.

claim: No study has tested hypotheses-in-rows vs columns in an LLM; evidence on LLM layout is indirect.
agent_test: This is the direct experiment to run.

claim: Cell-by-cell scoring in the ACH layout is argued to hamper thinking about dependencies between evidence; argued, not tested. Gap search found no test of cell-by-cell vs holistic scoring for dependent evidence; essay-scoring data show holistic agreement is higher than trait-by-trait (QWK 0.6 vs 0.2-0.4).
agent_test: Compare per-cell scoring to holistic per-hypothesis scoring.

claim: Judgmental coherence (additivity) was not affected by layout (F(2,160)=1.22, p=.299) and did not separate good from poor performers; 91.9% of analysts nonadditive.
agent_test: Check whether the agent's probabilities sum to 1 and if it matters.

claim: Pipelines that build an evidence graph for analysts raised classification F1 (0.65 to 0.81, 0.72 to 0.78, 0.56 to 0.65).
agent_test: Compare graph vs table store for evidence.

claim: In the 2016 single-matrix pilot (hypotheses as columns, N=64) 47.6% used a confirm-only strategy and 47.6% a balanced one; 48.4% chose A on Task 1.
agent_test: Use 45 to 60% as the human reference rate for confirm-only on Task 1 when testing the agent.

claim: All 11 tested LLMs favour confirming tests in a rule-discovery game; a higher share of incompatible tests goes with higher success; Dual-Goal prompting raised success in 8 of 11 setups and rule discovery from 42% to 56%.
agent_test: Add a disconfirming-test instruction at S4 and measure the I:C ratio of the agent's tests.

claim: Chain of thought does not remove sensitivity to meaning-preserving prompt changes: for Claude Opus 4.5 it cut the perturbation drop only from 2.79% to 2.38%; perturbations explain up to half of performance variance; no study measures spread over layouts for reasoning models.
agent_test: Measure format spread of the S4 prompt on our own model; report a range, not one format.

claim: The 2016 OSF data cannot check the 2024 per-layout counts; the raw 2024 data must be requested from the authors.
agent_test: None for the agent; keep per-layout percentages marked unverified.

claim: Display-organization theory (Kleinmuntz and Schkade 1993; Schkade and Kleinmuntz 1994, 60 MBA, 8 loans x 4 attributes) says layout changes which strategy is cheap, so layout can steer strategy; the originals do not predict a hypothesis-row advantage.
agent_test: Treat layout as a strategy steer: pick the layout that makes whole-hypothesis comparison cheap, then test.

claim: No replication, preregistered follow-up, sequential-vs-one-shot test or non-student replication of the row-layout effect was found by search on 2026-11-10.
agent_test: Run the agent test with sequential per-hypothesis calls vs one-shot matrix at equal tokens.

claim: Nearest LLM data on decomposed vs holistic judging (essay scoring) favours holistic agreement with humans (QWK about 0.6 vs 0.2-0.4 analytic); no test of a normalizing orientation step on evidence matrices exists; NORM for tables (58.66 vs 59.50) remains the only normalization evidence.
agent_test: Compare holistic per-hypothesis scoring with cell-by-cell scoring on ARC and BrainTeaser items before adopting cells.
